description: Linux system administration from installation to a hardened, monitored server: the shell and file system, scripting, users and permissions, backups, networking and remote access, package management, web and DNS services, security and performance. Taught to the depth of the professional Linux administration certifications and the standard text on the practice of system administration.
modelledOn: Nemeth, Snyder, Hein, Whaley and Mackin, UNIX and Linux System Administration Handbook
Linux Professional Institute LPIC-1 and Red Hat RHCSA objectives
Limoncelli, Hogan and Chalup, The Practice of System and Network Administration
outcomes: Install Linux with a planned partition layout, including dual boot, and manage the boot process and services.
Work fluently in the shell with files, directories, text editors and the standard text-processing tools.
Write shell scripts that automate administrative tasks safely.
Administer users, groups, permissions and ACLs and design a backup and recovery scheme.
Configure networking, SSH remote administration, package installation, an Apache web server and a DNS server.
Secure, troubleshoot and tune a Linux server and document its configuration.

units.title: System administration concepts
topics: The role of the system administrator; services, users, change, documentation, ethics
Linux history and distributions (openSUSE, Debian/Ubuntu, Red Hat family); the kernel, GNU userland, init systems
Virtual lab setup; snapshots as a safety net
Getting help: man, info, --help, documentation and communities

units.title: Linux installation, partitioning and dual boot
topics: Planning: hardware, partitions (/, /home, /var, swap), file systems (ext4, XFS, Btrfs), LVM
Installing openSUSE and a second distribution; YaST; dual boot with Windows and GRUB
The boot process: firmware, GRUB, kernel, systemd targets; rescue mode
Post-install: updates, time zone, locale, hostname, basic security

units.title: Files, directories and the shell
topics: The file system hierarchy standard; absolute and relative paths; hidden files; links
Core commands: ls, cd, cp, mv, rm, mkdir, find, locate, du, df, tar, gzip, mount
The shell: redirection, pipes, globbing, quoting, variables, history, aliases; job control
Text processing: cat, less, head, tail, grep, sort, uniq, cut, tr, wc, sed, awk; regular expressions
Text editors: vim and nano; configuring the editor

units.title: Shell scripts
topics: Bash scripting: shebang, variables, arguments, exit codes, conditionals, loops, functions
Input and output, here documents, command substitution, arithmetic
Error handling, set -euo pipefail, logging, cron and systemd timers for scheduling
Scripts for user creation, log rotation, backups and health checks; ShellCheck
Python as an administration language in brief

units.title: Users and groups, permissions and ACLs
topics: /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /etc/group; useradd, usermod, passwd, chage; password policies
Ownership and mode bits; chmod, chown, umask; setuid, setgid, sticky bit
sudo configuration and least privilege
POSIX ACLs with getfacl and setfacl; extended attributes; disk quotas

units.title: Backup and recovery
topics: Backup strategy: full, incremental, differential; 3-2-1 rule; retention; testing restores
Tools: tar, rsync, dd, snapshots with LVM and Btrfs, restic or borg
Recovering deleted files, broken boot loaders and forgotten root passwords
Disaster recovery planning for a small organisation with unreliable power

units.title: Network communications and remote administration
topics: Network configuration: ip, NetworkManager, static and DHCP addressing, /etc/hosts, resolv.conf
Diagnostics: ping, traceroute, ss, dig, tcpdump, nmap
SSH: server configuration, key-based login, agent, tunnels, scp and sftp; disabling password login
Remote management at scale: parallel SSH, Ansible in brief
Firewall with firewalld or nftables; NAT and port forwarding

units.title: Installing software packages
topics: Package managers: zypper and RPM, apt and dpkg; repositories, signing, dependencies
Building from source: configure, make, make install; checkinstall
Containers and Flatpak/Snap as alternative delivery; language package managers (pip, npm)
Keeping systems patched; unattended upgrades; vulnerability tracking

units.title: Apache web server and DNS
topics: Apache installation, configuration files, virtual hosts, directories, modules, logs; serving PHP
HTTPS with Let's Encrypt; redirects and basic authentication; Nginx as a comparison
BIND DNS server: forward and reverse zones, records, caching and forwarding, zone transfers
Testing DNS with dig and nslookup; common misconfigurations
Other services in brief: NFS and Samba file sharing, mail, databases

units.title: Security, troubleshooting and performance tuning
topics: Hardening: minimal services, SSH, firewall, updates, fail2ban, AppArmor or SELinux, auditing and logs
Troubleshooting method: logs (journalctl, /var/log), dmesg, strace, resource checks
Performance: top, htop, vmstat, iostat, sar; CPU, memory, disk and network bottlenecks; tuning sysctl and services
Monitoring with Nagios, Zabbix or Prometheus; documentation and runbooks
Capstone: build, secure and document a complete departmental server

schedule.title: The administrator's role and Linux basics
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page description of a sysadmin's duties in a small Kumasi company, compare three Linux distribution families, and list where you would look for help on a failing service.

tasks.title: Use man, info and --help in the virtual terminal to find the option that makes ls sort by size, and record the commands used
Identify the distribution, kernel version, init system and package manager of a given virtual machine using only shell commands, and record the output
Take a snapshot of a lab VM, deliberately break a system file, roll back to the snapshot, and show the file is restored

schedule.title: Installation, partitioning and boot
schedule.exercise: Design a disk layout for a 500 GB office server with separate /home and /var, justify the file system choices, and describe each stage of the boot process.

tasks.title: Create two partitions and a swap area on a blank virtual disk, format them with ext4, mount them, and verify with df and lsblk
Create an LVM volume group from two disks, make a logical volume, extend it by 2 GB while mounted, and confirm the file system grows
Boot a lab VM with a broken GRUB entry into rescue mode, repair the configuration, and confirm the default target is reached

schedule.title: File system and the shell
schedule.exercise: Explain the purpose of ten top-level directories in the file system hierarchy, then write one pipeline that finds the five largest files under /var/log.

tasks.title: Create a nested directory tree, copy and move files within it, and use find and du to locate the three biggest files
Create hard and symbolic links to a file, delete the original, and show which link still works using ls -li
Compose a pipeline with redirection and quoting that archives all .log files older than 7 days to a dated tar.gz, and verify its contents

schedule.title: Text processing and editors
schedule.exercise: Write a pipeline using grep, awk, sort and uniq to count failed SSH logins per source address from a log file, and explain each stage.

tasks.title: Use grep with a regular expression to find all lines containing an IPv4 address in a given log and count them with wc
Use awk and sort to total bytes transferred per client from a web log and list the top five clients
Use sed to rewrite a configuration file in place replacing a port number and commenting out a line, and prove the edit with diff

schedule.title: Bash scripting
schedule.exercise: Write a script that takes a directory argument, checks it exists, and prints the number of files and total size, with sensible exit codes and error messages.

tasks.title: Write a script with a shebang that takes a name argument, prints a greeting, and exits with status 1 if no argument is given
Write a script that reads a list of hostnames from a here document and pings each, printing a one-line status per host
Add set -euo pipefail, logging and a cron entry to a cleanup script, then force a failure and confirm the log shows the error

schedule.title: Administration scripts
schedule.exercise: Design a script to create 30 student accounts from a CSV file with home directories and a first-login password change, covering errors and duplicates.

tasks.title: Write a script that creates five users from a list, sets a default shell, and verifies the entries exist in /etc/passwd
Write a health check script reporting disk use, memory and failed services, and exiting non-zero when disk use passes 90 percent
Write a Python script that parses an authentication log, summarises failed logins per user and address, and flags more than 10 failures

schedule.title: Users, permissions and sudo
schedule.exercise: Plan the accounts, groups, permissions and sudo rules for a department of 20 staff and a shared project directory, and justify each rule against least privilege.

tasks.title: Create a user with a home directory, set a password policy with chage, lock the account, and verify the entry in /etc/shadow
Set up a shared directory with setgid and sticky bit so group members can add files but not delete each other's, and test with two users
Use ACLs and a disk quota to let one extra user read a project folder and limit another to 100 MB, then verify both rules

schedule.title: Backup and recovery
schedule.exercise: Design a backup plan for a small clinic with 3 servers and frequent power cuts, applying the 3-2-1 rule, giving retention periods and a restore test schedule.

tasks.title: Create a tar.gz backup of a directory, delete the directory, restore it from the archive, and verify with a checksum comparison
Use rsync to make a full backup and two incremental backups with hard links, and compare the disk space used by each
Recover a lab VM whose root password is forgotten and whose boot loader is damaged, documenting each step in a recovery log

schedule.title: Networking, SSH and firewalls
schedule.exercise: Document the network configuration, SSH hardening choices and firewall rules for a two-server office, and diagnose a case where a service is up but unreachable.

tasks.title: Set a static IP, gateway and DNS server on a lab VM with the ip command and a config file, and verify with ping and ip route
Set up key-based SSH login between two VMs, disable password login, and confirm that a password attempt is rejected
Configure a Linux router with NAT and a port forward to an internal web server, then verify access from outside with tests

schedule.title: Package management and patching
schedule.exercise: Compare how to install, query and remove software with zypper and apt, and write a patching policy for a set of servers including testing, windows and rollback.

tasks.title: Install, query, update and remove a package using the package manager and list the files and dependencies it brought in
Add a third-party repository with its signing key, install a package from it, and show the signature check passes
Configure unattended security upgrades on a lab VM, simulate a pending update, and verify it applies and logs the result

schedule.title: Web and DNS servers
schedule.exercise: Plan a web server serving two sites from one machine with HTTPS and basic authentication on an admin area, and write the DNS zone records needed for both.

tasks.title: Install Apache, publish a static page from a custom directory, and verify it loads from a second VM using curl
Configure two virtual hosts on one Apache server and confirm each name serves a different page with curl using Host headers
Set up a BIND server with forward and reverse zones for a small domain and verify the lookups from a client with dig

schedule.title: DNS testing and other services
schedule.exercise: Diagnose three broken DNS configurations from dig output, and plan file sharing with NFS for Linux and Samba for Windows clients in a computer lab.

tasks.title: Use dig and nslookup to query A, MX and NS records for a lab domain and explain each field of the answer section
Find and fix three planted DNS errors (missing dot, wrong serial, bad CNAME) in a zone file using named-checkzone and dig
Export a directory over NFS with read-only and read-write clients, mount it on two VMs, and verify the permissions behave as configured

schedule.title: Hardening, troubleshooting, monitoring and capstone
schedule.exercise: Write a runbook for a departmental server covering build, hardening checklist, monitoring thresholds, backup and restore procedures, and a triage guide for common failures.

tasks.title: Disable unused services, enable the firewall, and install fail2ban on a lab VM, then verify with ss and the firewall rule list
Diagnose a lab VM with a failing web service by reading journalctl, checking ports and disk, and fix the single planted fault
Find which of CPU, memory or disk is the bottleneck on a loaded VM using vmstat and iostat, tune one setting, and show the improvement
Build, harden and document a complete departmental server with web, DNS, backup and monitoring, and pass a test checklist of 15 items
